shanghaitech_density_vs_performance.verdict: density does NOT explain the per-scene ordering -- consistent with H2 (mismatch in the KIND of anomaly), not H1 (sparsity alone)

suited_to: Collective, crowd-scale events where a large fraction of visible people change motion together (UMN-style escape/panic).
Dense scenes: validated at ~15 persons/frame; every zone-level feature is defined only when a zone is occupied.
Lead times up to k=30 frames (1s at 30fps) by the stricter sign test; point estimates stay above chance further out but are not individually significant.
Fixed-camera continuous feeds -- the running normalizers assume a stable viewpoint and are reset at every scene boundary.
not_suited_to: Individual or small-group anomalies (a lone cyclist, a 2-5 person altercation). ShanghaiTech scene 05 scores BELOW chance at every horizon -- these events do not move a crowd-level aggregate, and can push it the wrong way.
Sparse scenes (~4 persons/frame): most spatial zones are empty, leaving direction_entropy and stop_ratio undefined ~62%/67% of the time within occupied zones.
Moving or newly-installed cameras: the per-clip running normalizers need time to stabilise after every reset.
Any deployment needing a calibrated probability rather than a ranking -- all reported metrics are threshold-free (AUROC/AUPRC).
